items.detail: Fetch and lock an RFC's plain text or RFCXML v3 source, read it into one document model, and extract its BCP 14 requirements with cited spans; RFC 9220 is the RFCXML test case. Held by crates/rfcspec-cli/tests/rfcxml.rs.
items.label: Plain text and RFCXML

items.detail: Every RFC the index publishes as RFCXML or plain text, with its requirement counts by level and section and its RFCXML references, unreviewed. Held by task bulk.
items.label: The whole RFC index

items.detail: RFC 868, RFC 6455, RFC 1035 and RFC 5905: a reviewed overlay, lowered models that pass bounded exploration, and a generated codec crate with its tests. Held by task time, task websocket, task dns, task ntp.
items.label: Four profiles end to end

items.detail: Status proposals from a model, recorded with their cited spans, settled by review into the overlay and replayed offline in the gate. Held by task websocket.
items.label: Recorded proposals and review

items.detail: Search and filter the RFC index, open an RFC's requirements by section, update graph and references, and see a profiled RFC's reviewed layer. Held by task explorer.
items.label: The RFC explorer

items.detail: RFC 5234 and RFC 7405 ABNF parsed, references resolved to rules, core rules and RFC imports, and input matched against a rule. Held by crates/rfcspec-abnf/tests/rfc6455_core.rs.
items.label: ABNF parse, resolve and match

items.detail: Each section's ABNF figures collected into one catalogue grammar, from plain text and RFCXML. Held by crates/rfcspec-wire/tests/grammars.rs.
items.label: Catalogue grammars

items.detail: An RFC becomes requirements, grammars, layouts, registries, defined procedures and limits, each with a source span and a digest (design D1).
items.label: The catalogue, rfcspec/1

items.detail: Machines lower to ess-protospec/1, message and value types and registries to an ess/N system; what ESS cannot carry is listed as a gap (design D2).
items.label: ESS as the target

items.detail: Bytes and bits live in rfcspec-wire/1: ABNF verbatim, bit-level ABNF and packet layouts (design D3).
items.label: A wire-format sidecar

items.detail: One value per axis for each protocol layer: unit, delivery, direction, multiplexing, exchange, correlation, lifetime, layering, roles (design D4).
items.label: Communication semantics

items.detail: Model output is a recorded proposal with cited spans, replayed offline; no gate calls a model (design D5, D6).
items.label: AI proposes, review decides

items.detail: Wire protocols, data formats, extensions and registries are modelled; algorithms as signatures with test vectors; the rest get a requirement catalogue (design D11).
items.label: Which kinds of RFC are modelled

items.detail: What remains of M0: defined terms in the catalogue, and a survey classifying every RFC in the index by kind.
items.label: Defined terms and a survey by kind

items.detail: What remains of M1: the RFC 2616 and bit-level ABNF dialects, packet diagrams read into layouts, the RFC 6455 frame agreement check, and the handshake codec and frame codec vectors.
items.label: The rest of the wire layer

items.detail: What remains of M2: recorded proposals for the parties, the communication semantics and the WebSocket machines; status proposals, review and lowering are shipped.
items.label: Proposals for parties, semantics and machines

items.detail: What remains of M3: machine, limits and roles in the generated crate, an Autobahn run and a recorded requirement matrix; the frame codec is shipped.
items.label: A generated WebSocket core

items.detail: What remains of M4: concurrent sessions, and the ESS gap proposals G1, G3 and G4 with WebSocket and DNS as evidence; the header codec and query machine are shipped.
items.label: Concurrent DNS sessions and the gap proposals

items.detail: The WebSocket codec as a pure WASM module and a websocket channel port in a Spindle environment.
items.label: RFCspec cores in Spindle

items.detail: TCP as the hard case: sequence-number arithmetic, windows and timers from measurements.
items.label: A transport
